entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Possidius of Calama was a 5th-century bishop of the Roman province of Numidia, known for his friendship with the influential theologian Augustine of Hippo. Born into a Christian family in the 4th century, Possidius rose to become bishop of Calama in 390 CE, a position he held until his death in 437 CE. During his tenure, Possidius wrote a biography of Augustine and compiled an indiculus, a list of his works.

Possidius' significance lies in his role as a bridge between the early Christian community and the wider Roman world. His friendship with Augustine and his writings about the saint have provided valuable insights into the theological debates of the time.

The legacy of Possidius can be seen in the continued importance of his biography and indiculus, which have been studied by scholars for centuries. His work on Augustine has helped to shape our understanding of the saint's thought and influence, and has contributed to the development of Christian theology.

In the world of 5th-century Christianity, Possidius' work had a lasting impact on the development of doctrine and practice. His writings about Augustine have been widely studied and continue to inform theological debates today.

Possidius' story is a testament to the power of friendship and the importance of preserving the works of influential thinkers. His biography and indiculus remain essential sources for understanding the early Christian church and its leaders.

One striking statistic about Possidius is that he was one of the earliest Christian writers to use the term 'Augustinianism' to describe the theological debates of the time.
